text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Supreme Court rules as illegal the railway workers' strike that is now into its 13th day.

- During the process of its rehabilitation Privredna Banka Zagreb to write off 704 million kuna debts of firms located in the liberated and still occupied sections of the country, while it is looking to retrive 540 million kuna from firms in former Yugoslav states.

- Some 6.8 billion kuna to be allocated for the setting-up of a new social welfare programe between 1997 and 1999. The new program to be based on lasting solutions in line with the future expected rise in the standard of living.
- Initial figures show that 1996 will be the fifth year in a row of negative natality trends. Results for the first eight months of 1996 have shown 2,820 more people dying than being born.
- U.S. Embassy in Zagreb and USAID launch a program of assisstance for local authorities in towns across Croatia with an emphasis on financing of housing projects.
- Some 60 tons of dangerous waste owned by the Pliva pharmaceutical company is being transported around Croatia between Bjelovar and Zagreb with no solution in sight.
- Croatian Army to be set-up according to western standards, says in an interview general Pavao Miljevac, Croatian Army Chief-of-Staff. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
